national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that the government is fully committed to creating a modern sports ecosystem for India in the 21st century. He said that, from sports universities to modern training centres, an ecosystem is being developed across the country where talent receives support at every stage. Addressing the Khelo India Dialogue through video conferencing today, Mr Modi said that sports is not limited merely to winning medals, rather, it is a mission to unite India’s sporting prowess and youth power in the building of a developed India. He said every district has the potential to shine on the global sports map. The Prime Minister said he had announced from the ramparts of the Red Fort that a big talent hunt to identify kids from 5 to 15 years of age in sports. He emphasised the need to focus not only on the sport a child is interested in but also on identifying the sport they are best suited for. The Prime Minister assured to provide all possible support from the government for this. The Prime Minister expressed happiness that today sports has emerged as an excellent career and profession in India. Mr Modi said sports does not just teach to become champions but also to become better competitors. He said, ‘The Khelo India Samvad is not merely a program for discussing sports, but it is a platform for dialogue where every single idea can give a new direction to the nation’s sports vision. ‘Prime Minister said that these new ideas from the power of the country’s youth will become the strength that helps realise the vision of Viksit Bharat. Speaking on the occasion, Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Mansukh Mandaviya said that under the leadership of Prime Minister Modi, sports has emerged as a national priority and an important instrument of youth empowerment. He said India’s sports ecosystem is now moving beyond infrastructure and medals as initiatives such as the Fit India Movement and Sunday on Cycle encourage citizens to make fitness a part of everyday life. The Minister said that the National Sports Governance Act is promoting transparency and accountability and strengthening fair opportunities in sports so that talented sportspersons receive an equal platform to demonstrate their abilities. Dr Mandaviya said the government’s approach is aimed at making India’s youth active partners in the journey towards a Viksit Bharat. The Programme was organised as part of the National Sports Day 2026 celebrations by Mera Yuva Bharat (MY Bharat). It was conducted across the country with participation of youth at two colleges in every district across States and Union Territories. The event brought together sports, youth leadership, civic responsibility, volunteering, fitness and nation-building on a common platform. The Khelo India Dialogue provided a direct channel for young people to engage with the country’s sporting ambitions while ensuring that their ideas and perspectives become part of the continuing conversation on India’s youth and sports ecosystem. The Khelo India Dialogue is being held in line with Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision of building a fit, disciplined and sporting nation and placing the aspirations of youth at the centre of the national development agenda.

national_raw_news.title: 5 hours ago | International 679 Nepal flash flood claims nearly 160 lives; over 750 Missing, including 133 Indians
national_raw_news.content: In Nepal, nearly 160 people have been killed and over 750, including 133 Indian nationals, remain missing after a massive flash flood swept through central Nepal yesterday. Originating in Tibet, the flood devastated several towns and villages, washing away critical bridges and crippling a dozen hydropower projects. Nepal Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal told the parliament that an earthquake hit the Tibet region at 8:37 am (local time) and the flash floods were reported three minutes later, suggesting a glacial outburst due to tremors, which triggered the floods. Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said the massive flood entered the Trishuli River through the Bhote Koshi in Timure, a border town in Rasuwa district, due to the rockslide and swelling of the Lhende River situated along the Nepal-Tibet border. It then spread along the river course to other districts like Nuwakot, Chitwan, Gorkha, Tanahu and Nawalparasi East, covering areas ranging to nearly 2 hundred kilometres from the capital Kathmandu. The Nepal Police in a social media post said 157 people died in the flash flood. The Nepal government said around 500 people were missing. According to China’s state-run news channel, 3 people were dead and 265 were missing on the Chinese side of the border. Videos from the affected areas showed a powerful surge of muddy water, rocks and debris sweeping through the border region. Officials said that around 100 people have been rescued from different parts of the affected areas. Of them, 30 are undergoing treatment at Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital in Kathmandu. Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke to his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah and assured him of all possible humanitarian assistance. Mr Shah thanked Prime Minister Modi for his warm words of solidarity and for offering humanitarian assistance. New Delhi has already sent the first tranche of relief supplies to the neighbouring nation. The Indian Embassy in Kathmandu issued emergency numbers for assistance and information related to Indian nationals. The numbers are: +977 985 131 6807 and +977 970 910 7500. The Nepal Tourism Board also issued similar numbers, including the toll-free emergency number 1234, hotline 1144 and Tourist Police number 9851289445 for help. The Embassy of India in Beijing also issued a helpline number – 0086 185 1428 4905, which can also be contacted through WhatsApp. At least 50 of the Indians missing were pilgrims for the Kailash Manasarovar Yatra. Several Indian states – including Uttar Pradesh and Keralam have also issued helpline numbers. Other than the Indians and NRIs, the remaining missing tourists were from more than two dozen countries, including the US, Malaysia, the UK, South Africa, Australia and the Netherlands. Foreign Minister of Nepal, Shisir Khanal, informed the House of Representatives that 80 security personnel, including 44 Nepal Army personnel, have gone missing from various locations. The flash flood damaged eight operational hydropower projects with a total capacity of 354 megawatts and five under-construction projects located in the Nuwakot and Rasuwa districts. Nineteen motorable bridges have been washed away. Nepalese Army, Armed Police Force and Nepal Police personnel have been mobilised in the affected areas to carry out rescue and relief work. Chinese President Xi Jinping ordered all-out efforts to search for and rescue missing people. A total of 145 officers and soldiers from the Xigaze detachment of the People’s Armed Police have been sent to the affected border port to assist with emergency response operations. Mr Xi also stressed the need to strengthen monitoring and early warning, ensure scientific rescue operations and guard against secondary disasters. Nepalese President Ramchandra Paudel has expressed sorrow over the loss of lives and property due to the flash flood.

national_raw_news.title: 5 hours ago | National 114 Centre begins targeted release of onions from buffer stocks to ensure adequate availability &...
national_raw_news.content: The Government has commenced calibrated and targeted release of onions from the buffer stock to ensure adequate availability and moderate seasonal price pressures in the coming months. The Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution has said that onion availability is comfortable to meet domestic demand in the coming months, as estimated production of onions for 2025-26 is over 307 Lakh Metric Tonnes (LMT). It added that in view of the comfortable production outlook, the Government has fixed a procurement target of two lakh metric tonnes of Rabi onion for the Price Stabilisation Fund (PSF) buffer during 2026-27. The procurement operation commenced on the 15th of May and around 1.21 LMT of onions have been procured for the buffer. The Ministry added that onions will be sold at 35 rupees per kilogram through mobile vans and retail outlets of the National Cooperative Consumers Federation (NCCF) and the National Agricultural Cooperative Marketing Federation (NAFED), as well as through Safal and Kendriya Bhandar outlets. The Ministry said the first Kanda Express has left Nashik and is expected to reach Delhi NCR with about 800 metric tonnes of onions late evening today or by tomorrow morning. Simultaneously, supplies are being moved through road transport to other major consumption centres across the country.

national_raw_news.title: Northeast Power Ministers seek greater funding from centre for modernising regional power grid 1 hour ago 16
national_raw_news.content: Power ministers of the Northeastern states have sought greater financial assistance from the Centre for modernising the regional power grid and implementing key projects to improve electricity supply in the region, an official statement released yesterday said. The demand was raised at a meeting with Union Power Minister Manohar Lal Khattar in New Delhi on Tuesday. Led by North Eastern Regional Power Committee (NERPC) Chairman and Meghalaya Power Minister Metbah Lyngdoh, the delegation included Mizoram Power Minister F Rodingliana, Arunachal Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Chowna Mein and senior officials from the northeastern states. The ministers urged the Centre to provide the funds required for grid modernisation and sought special assistance for projects already submitted by the states under the Power System Development Fund (PSDF), following changes in the scheme’s implementation, the statement said. They also highlighted priority projects for the region, including Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) or Energy Management System (EMS) and Emergency Restoration System (ERS), and sought central support for their implementation, it said. The ministers apprised of the difficulties faced by the Northeastern states in executing power infrastructure projects due to the region’s challenging terrain. They said that long transmission lines are often required to supply electricity to remote and scattered settlements, making reliable power supply difficult and stressed the need for additional substations in far-flung areas. Rodingliana urged Khattar to formulate a mechanism for more transparent and effective utilisation of the 10 per cent Gross Budgetary Support (GBS) earmarked for the Northeast by 54 Union ministries. He also sought a larger allocation from the 10 per cent GBS specifically for development of the power sector in the region. Khattar said he would take up the funding requirements raised by the Northeastern states with the Union Finance Minister, according to the statement. However, he noted that the Centre may not be able to bear the entire cost of all proposed projects and the states would also have to contribute, it said. The states’ capacity to contribute would have to be assessed before a comprehensive proposal is prepared and pursued with the Ministry of Finance, Khattar said. The Union Power Minister also urged the states to expedite the ongoing installation of smart meters and stressed the need for “check meters” to help consumers verify and understand smart-meter readings. He further called for sustained efforts to reduce transmission losses and promote commercialisation in the power sector wherever feasible. The NERPC was constituted under the Ministry of Power in accordance with the Electricity Act, 2003, and comprises the seven Northeastern states. Its chairmanship rotates among the member states.
